citations.quote: An external scalar datum consists of a spin-zero species assigned a mass $m>0$ and elastic two-particle threshold $s=4m^2$. This is a mathematical input package; it does not construct a one-particle scattering state or a scattering matrix.

A local operator in this finite-order data is an element of $P_{r,q,D}$ evaluated at $x$ on the $r$-jet of the fields. A scalar operator invariant under the declared symmetries is an element of $V_{r,q,D}=P_{r,q,D}^{G}$. Engineering dimension means this assigned mass weight; it is not a statement about an observed quantity. In four dimensions a term with operator $\mathcal O_D$ has the convention $C\mathcal O_D/\Lambda^{D-4}$, where $\Lambda$ has mass dimension one and $C$ is dimensionless.

citations.quote: Define the first nonconstant even forward coefficient by $c_1=B''(0)/2!$, of mass dimension $-4$. Exact matching at $\mu_*$ is a supplied datum of the form $$c_1=\frac{4C_8(\mu_*)}{\Lambda^4}+\Delta_{\mathrm{match}},$$ where $\Delta_{\mathrm{match}}\in\mathbb R$ has mass dimension $-4$ and contains every other contribution to this exact $v^2$ coefficient, including other operators, loops, and matching or truncation effects.

The real operator $\mathcal O_8=(\partial_\mu\phi\,\partial^\mu\phi)^2$ is then a local scalar of engineering dimension eight. Its coefficient in a chosen local representative is written $$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{EFT}}=-\frac12\partial_\mu\phi\,\partial^\mu\phi-\frac12m^2\phi^2+\frac{C_8(\mu_*)}{\Lambda^4}\mathcal O_8+\cdots,$$

Also require $B$ to extend continuously from each open half-plane onto every compact segment of either real cut bank avoiding $\pm\nu_0$. This is an extra admissibility assumption on the supplied data, not a consequence of finite pointwise boundary values or a claim about every quantum field theory.
